summary: Five Islands lighthouse (1914) on Minas Basin: wooden tower moved four times, kept by the MacBurnie family 1914-1963, deactivated 1993, now in a park at Broderick Lane.

lens.note: Fourth-order dioptric lens fixed white 1922-1941 (NSLPS); flashing red 4 s on a fourth-order dioptric lens from 1992 (NSLPS)

structures.note: Built winter 1913-14 at Sand Point (Colchester registry); about 10 m (33 ft) high (NSLPS; Rowlett gives 10 m / 30 ft); painted white with red trim; moved 1952, 1957, 1996 and 2008
Combined wooden lighthouse and dwelling under contract, 1913-14 (Lighthouse Friends; Marine annual reports)

staffing.note: Keeper service ended in 1967 with the light on the power grid (Lighthouse Friends; Colchester registry)

access.note: Five Islands Lighthouse Park at the end of Broderick Lane. Sources differ on whether the tower can be entered: Lighthouse Friends says open afternoons in summer; the Lighthouse Directory says site open, tower closed, interior closed since 2019

facts.agency: Municipality of the County of Colchester (Five Islands Lighthouse Park); managed by the Five Islands Lighthouse Preservation Society

events.note: Contract with A. L. Mury of West Arichat, $750, for a combined wooden lighthouse and dwelling at Sand Point
Cyrus A. MacBurnie hired as first keeper on 6 April 1914
Fourth-order dioptric lens, fixed white, seasonal April-January, 1922-1941
Moved back from the eroding shore
Moved back again, placed as far inland as the property allowed
Oil lamp removed and battery system installed (about 1963)
Changed from white to red when electricity reached Sand Point
Flashing red (4 s), fourth-order dioptric lens, electric (NSLPS). Conflicts with the 1967 red change in the Colchester registry
Winter 1995-96 storm undercut the concrete retaining wall; the wall collapsed
Bought by the municipality (Colchester registry) or a community group (Lighthouse Friends); moved onto Sand Point Campground
Five Islands Lighthouse Preservation Society formed
Moved 6 November 2008 on a flatbed about 7 km to Broderick Lane, after the campground was sold at auction
Society awarded the Craig Harding Lighthouse Preservation Award, 28 April 2010
Registered as a municipal heritage property, July 2013
Interior closed because the ladder to the gallery had deteriorated

corrections.why: The record note cites the Lighthouse Directory as saying the site is open, but that same directory says the site is open and the tower closed, and that the interior has been closed since 2019 because the gallery ladder deteriorated. Lighthouse Friends' summer-opening description is older. Needs a human check before publication.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Wikidata gives active; the Lighthouse Directory, Lighthouse Friends, NSLPS and the Colchester registry all say deactivated in 1993 and no longer operating. Inactive kept.

Lighthouse Friends says built in 1913; the Colchester registry says the building went up in the winter of 1913 to 1914 and was first lit in 1914; the Marine report year ended 31 March 1914 lists the contract. Built 1913-14 and first lit 1914 kept.
Lighthouse Friends' roster gives Cyrus MacBurnie from 1905, but its own text and the 1915 Marine list give 6 April 1914. The 1914 start is kept.
Lighthouse Friends: summer afternoons, tower open in season. Lighthouse Directory: site open, tower closed, interior closed since 2019. Both are kept in the story.
The Colchester registry says the light changed from white to red in 1967; NSLPS dates flashing red to 1992. Both kept.
Lighthouse Friends credits a community group; the Colchester registry says the municipality purchased it. Both kept.

The record's point (45.405374, -64.088575) is the 2008 Broderick Lane site. The tower stood at Sand Point from 1914 to 1996 and at Sand Point Campground from 1996 to 2008. NSLPS gives the campground position as 45 deg 24 min 21 sec N, 64 deg 05 min 15 sec W. The record's point is correct for the present site and is not an error.
NSLPS gives the tower as 33 ft (about 10 m); Rowlett gives 30 ft (10 m). The story gives both figures and keeps 'about 10 m'.

notes_for_editor: Fact-check 2026-10-27 (55 quotes found on the first run). Removed 'north shore of Minas Basin' and 'small' (no source; Minas Basin is what NSLPS and Lighthouse Friends give). Removed 'led by residents' (Lighthouse Friends says 'led a community group'; the two named leaders are not named in the story). Stated the county/municipality buyer disagreement and the 1967 vs 1992 colour disagreement in the text, the 30 vs 33 ft height, and Lighthouse Friends' 1905 roster start. Footnote for the 1914 report now gives printed p. 39 (scan 46). Mill/tower access conflict kept, with a note not to assume the tower is open. The $750 contract to A. L. Mury was checked on the page image (printed p. 39, scan 46): the Five Islands row reads Contract, A. L. Mury, West Arichat, 750.00. Lighthouse Friends independently gives the same contractor and $750, so the match is supported, but C. A. McBurnie is on the Five Islands row of the 1915 keeper list (printed p. 69, scan 76), confirmed on the page image. The 1915 accounts-outstanding row (printed p. 41, scan 48) was checked on the page image: Five islands, $207.04. The 1915 report also has a 'Completion of work of the erection of a combined wooden lighthouse and dwelling started last year' entry (scan p.49, printed p.42) whose station was not checked. Lighthouse Friends' roster 1905 start for MacBurnie conflicts with its own text. The 1996 purchaser (community group vs municipality) and the 1967 vs 1992 colour change are unresolved. The Lighthouse Directory's 'tower closed' vs Lighthouse Friends' summer opening needs a site check. A hiking website gives '2,132 acres' for the Sand Point purchase, which is almost certainly a decimal slip for 2.132 acres (Colchester: just over 2 acres); not cited. Ronald MacBurnie and Anita Murphy are named in Lighthouse Friends as community leaders in 1996; they are not named in the story. A fundycontemplations blog gives a first keeper's wage of $115.67 and is a lead only.
